edits.old: The unofficial driver-compatibility checker README describes an automated check based on driver releases and a three-year server-EOL window. Use it as a candidate filter, then confirm each pairing in MongoDB's official matrix, which exposes full, partial, incompatible, or untested status and runtime details. (medium confidence)
edits.new: The driver-compatibility-checker README describes a static web app that checks driver versions against server EOL plus a 3-year support window, with driver data updated automatically by GitHub Actions from driver releases. Use it as a candidate filter, then confirm each pairing in MongoDB's official compatibility tables, which mark a driver/server pairing as fully compatible, partially compatible, incompatible, or untested and also list language runtime (e.g. Node.js, Java, CPython) compatibility. Sources: https://github.com/alexbevi/driver-compatibility-checker ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/compatibility.md

evidence.quote: It uses MongoDB's official support lifecycle policy, which mandates drivers support server versions up to 3 years beyond EOL.
This repository includes comprehensive GitHub Actions workflows to automatically keep both driver and server version data up-to-date:
| ⊛ | The driver version will work with the MongoDB version, but not all new MongoDB features are supported. |
| No mark | The driver version is not tested with the MongoDB version. |
| ✗ | The driver version will not work with the MongoDB version. Attempting to connect to the MongoDB version will result in errors. |
This section shows compatibility between versions of the Java driver and versions of Java.

edits.old: MongoDB states that driver and server version numbers advance independently, so matching similar version numbers does not establish compatibility. Before a major production upgrade, MongoDB recommends confirming driver support and testing the application; Percona independently recommends testing the new server version and verifying driver compatibility. (high confidence)

edits.old: Driver/server incompatibility has a protocol boundary: MongoDB's SDAM specification requires a driver to mark a topology incompatible and set a compatibility error when the server and client wire-version ranges do not overlap. The compatibility table separately distinguishes a partial feature set from a connection incompatibility or an untested combination. (high confidence)
edits.new: Driver/server incompatibility has a protocol boundary: MongoDB's SDAM specification requires a driver to mark a topology incompatible and set a compatibility error when the server and client wire-version ranges do not overlap. The compatibility table separately distinguishes a partial feature set from a connection incompatibility or an untested combination. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-discovery-and-monitoring.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/compatibility.md

evidence.quote: If any ServerDescription is incompatible, the client MUST set the TopologyDescription's "compatible" field to false and
minWireVersion > clientMaxWireVersion, or
| ⊛ | The driver version will work with the MongoDB version, but not all new MongoDB features are supported. |
| ✗ | The driver version will not work with the MongoDB version. Attempting to connect to the MongoDB version will result in errors. |
| No mark | The driver version is not tested with the MongoDB version. |

statements.statement: SDAM requires a driver to mark the topology incompatible and set a compatibility error when wire-version ranges do not overlap.
The compatibility table distinguishes partial feature set, connection incompatibility, and untested combinations.

edits.rationale: The SDAM spec defines incompatibility as non-overlapping wire-version ranges and requires setting compatible=false with a compatibilityError. MongoDB's compatibility page separately distinguishes partial support (⊛), non-working (✗) and untested (no mark) pairings.

edits.old: As of 2026-10-14, MongoDB's matrix marks Java Sync 5.12–5.13, Node.js 7.6–7.7, PyMongo 4.18, .NET/C# 3.10–3.12, and Go 2.9 fully compatible with MongoDB Server 9.0. MongoDB separately advises confirming that the driver supports the target server version before upgrading. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
